resources: Arfken & Weber; Boas
core_notes: A = A_x i + A_y j + A_z k. Its magnitude is |A| = sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2 + A_z^2). A unit vector is A_hat = A/|A| for A != 0.
A·B = |A||B|cos(theta) = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z. It is a scalar. The scalar projection of A on B is A·B_hat.
A×B is normal to the plane of A and B, with magnitude |A×B| = |A||B|sin(theta). It is anti-commutative: A×B = -B×A.
A·(B×C) is the signed volume of the parallelepiped formed by A, B and C. It is zero when the vectors are coplanar.
A×(B×C) = B(A·C) - C(A·B). Cross multiplication is not associative.
Work by a constant force is W = F·Delta r; torque is tau = r×F; angular momentum is L = r×p.
key_concepts: Represent vectors in Cartesian components and unit-vector bases.
Use dot and cross products for projections, angles, areas and torque.
Use scalar and vector triple products and interpret their geometry.
Recognize vector-product identities and common CSIR-NET traps.
formula_sheet: Vector projection of A on B = [(A·B)/|B|^2]B

worked_example_detail.title: Projection
worked_example_detail.problem: Find the scalar projection of A=(2,-1,2) on B=(1,2,2).
worked_example_detail.solution: A·B=4 and |B|=3, so the scalar projection is 4/3.

practice_v5_5.question: If A·B=0 for two nonzero vectors, the angle is:
practice_v5_5.explanation: A·B=|A||B|cos(theta)=0, hence theta=90°.

practice_v5_5.question: The magnitude of (i+j)×(i-j) is:
practice_v5_5.explanation: The cross product is -2k, whose magnitude is 2.

practice_v5_5.question: If A×B=0 for nonzero vectors, they are:
practice_v5_5.explanation: sin(theta)=0, so theta is 0 or 180 degrees.

practice_v5_5.question: The scalar triple product of three coplanar vectors is:
practice_v5_5.explanation: It represents signed volume, which vanishes for coplanar vectors.

practice_v5_5.question: Which identity is correct?
practice_v5_5.explanation: This is the vector triple-product identity.

practice_v5_5.question: A force F=3i+4j acts at r=2i-j. Find torque about the origin.
practice_v5_5.explanation: r×F has k component 2(4)-(-1)(3)=11.

practice_v5_5.question: For A=(1,1,0), B=(1,0,1), find a unit vector perpendicular to both.
practice_v5_5.explanation: A×B=(1,-1,-1). Normalize it.

practice_v5_5.question: Given |A|=2, |B|=3 and |A+B|=sqrt(19), find the angle.
practice_v5_5.explanation: 19=4+9+12cos(theta), so cos(theta)=1/2.

revision_v5_4.one_minute: Vector products encode projection, oriented area and volume; use identities carefully because the cross product is not associative.
